passages.h: It is a story about people.
passages.t: Our story. What started with a teacher listening to his students grew into an organization serving teachers, children, women and communities across Liberia. The beginning. Founding TIME Inc. Reaching rural Liberia. Training teachers. Mission & values. The people behind TIME.

As a classroom teacher, Dr. Philip V. Saywrayne, III began noticing things that concerned him deeply. Many students, particularly young women, struggled to keep up. Some submitted assignments late or not at all. Some slept during lectures. Some young men left campus before the school day had ended. These behaviors could easily have been read as a lack of seriousness. He believed there was more to the story. He began listening and later administered a diagnostic assessment to understand what was really happening. The answers were painful but important. Students were struggling to pay school fees, buy basic materials and meet daily needs. Some worked long, difficult hours just to remain in school. Some young women had become vulnerable to exploitative survival practices because of economic hardship; some young men were exposed to theft, substances and other risks.

Sometimes a student does not need another reprimand. Sometimes the student needs someone to listen, someone to care, and someone to help create a pathway through the difficulty. He and his wife began helping wherever they could. There was no organization, large budget or elaborate structure. They saw needs and responded with whatever they had: school supplies, encouragement and practical support, offered quietly and personally.

passages.h: From personal kindness to an institution
passages.t: As they heard more stories from young people, women, families and communities, it became clear that the need was far greater than two individuals could meet. The need also extended beyond the capital. Rural towns and villages had children without basic materials, teachers without professional support, and women and widows in need. That raised a simple question: if the needs are so great, and we are already trying to help, should there not be an organization through which this work can be organized, strengthened and continued?

passages.h: From personal kindness to an institution
passages.t: In January 2021 , the Technical Institute for Many Empowerment (TIME Inc.) was established and registered with the Government of Liberia. Dr. Saywrayne, his partner Ms. Tibeh E. Gbassagee-Saywrayne, and their daughter Ms. Tijue N. Suah developed the organization together and coined its name, a name for an institution that would not merely respond to immediate needs, but also empower people through education, professional development, skills training, humanitarian assistance and self-reliance. Our guiding Scripture. “Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in your power to act.”

passages.h: From personal kindness to an institution
passages.t: Proverbs 3:27 (NIV). We may not be able to solve every problem, but we can do something. And sometimes what seems small to us means a great deal to someone who has very little.

passages.h: Walking to where the need is
passages.t: The first organization to provide significant encouragement and support was WE-CARE Liberia . Through this partnership, TIME Inc. extended its outreach to underprivileged women, children, teachers and communities in rural and hard-to-reach areas of Grand Bassa, Bong and Margibi Counties . Children in a rural community hold up books delivered by the TIME Inc. team. We found children attending school without textbooks, copybooks or pencils, and schools with damaged chalkboards and too few benches. Improving education, we learned, sometimes requires physically showing up. We have walked two to three hours to reach remote villages, carrying textbooks, copybooks, pencils and stationery; we have replaced damaged chalkboards and repaired benches.

passages.h: Walking to where the need is
passages.t: Much of this has been made possible through our own limited resources and proceeds from the sale of books and educational materials. We have sometimes given from what we ourselves had, because we could not stand before a need and simply say, “We do not have enough.”

As TIME Inc. grew, its work expanded into structured educational and professional development. We are now an accredited supplementary teacher-training institution under the Bureau of Teacher Education, Ministry of Education. Many people possess substantial knowledge in a subject but have had little formal preparation in pedagogy. Our goal is to help subject specialists become skilled professional educators with a strong foundation in classroom management, lesson planning, instructional methods, assessment, educational leadership and professional ethics.

Our purpose is not simply to issue certificates. It is to develop teachers who know what they are doing, understand why they are doing it and can make a meaningful difference in the lives of their learners.

Educational problems rarely exist in isolation. A child who cannot afford a schoolbook may struggle academically. A student working long hours to pay fees arrives exhausted. A teacher who never received adequate preparation struggles to give learners the instruction they deserve. So we address education from a broader perspective.
A Liberia where every person, whatever their circumstances, can develop their God-given potential through education and opportunity.

To empower people through education, serve humanity with compassion, strengthen teachers through professional development, support vulnerable women and children, and extend learning to underserved communities.
Dignity, compassion, sacrifice, integrity and service, with humanity at the center of everything we do.

passages.h: A family that decided to serve
passages.t: The people behind TIME. Meet the founders, the principal of Phìtìa Academy and the lecturers who teach our programs. When we can help, let us help. When we can teach, let us teach. When we can encourage, let us encourage. When we can give, let us give. The spirit in which TIME Inc. was born, and continues to serve.

passages.h: A lifelong commitment to quality education
passages.t: About Dr. Saywrayne. Throughout his career, Dr. Saywrayne has worked to advance quality education, strengthen educational leadership and empower underserved communities through capacity-building. As Executive Director of TIME Inc., he leads teacher education, vocational and technical training, and outreach to underprivileged women, children and other vulnerable people in Bong, Grand Bassa and Margibi Counties. He has taught undergraduate and graduate students in Research Methodology, Education, English, Sociology and Educational Leadership at the University of Liberia, Carver Christian University, Cuttington University and Trinity University Graduate School, and has mentored many students, emerging scholars and school leaders.

Est. 2023 · Sister school. “We shape the mind that will shape the future.” PHICA was founded to support children whose lives were disrupted by the Ebola crisis. Location · Slagbaawein, Tower Hill, Lower Margibi County. Education district · Marshall Education District. Level · Nursery, Elementary & Junior High. Status · Registered with the Government of Liberia.

passages.h: Where others saw an empty field, the founders saw classrooms.
passages.t: Our beginning. Dr. Philip V. Saywrayne, III and Mrs. Tibeh E. Gbassagee-Saywrayne personally bought the land, an undeveloped field of savanna grass, and began building a school. They imagined a place where children could sit in classrooms, hold books, learn to read and write, discover their abilities and begin to imagine a different future. That vision became Phìtìa Academy. PHICA is more than a school building. It is a response to a need, an expression of hope, and a commitment to children whose circumstances should never determine the limits of their future.

Meet our principal. Principal, Phìtìa Academy (PHICA). A co-founder of TIME Inc. and Phìtìa Academy, Ms. Gbassagee serves as the school principal. She has helped support students and teachers from the very beginning.

passages.h: Children the Ebola crisis left behind
passages.t: The context. During and after the Ebola crisis, many children's education was interrupted for long periods. Some lost one or both parents and were raised by relatives, neighbors or the wider community. Others grew up in families already struggling with poverty. Before PHICA, a community school was doing its best, but it lacked trained, qualified teachers and resources. At one point, three shipping containers were being used as classrooms , including for children orphaned by Ebola. A shipping container can provide temporary shelter, but it cannot by itself provide the kind of educational environment every child deserves.

passages.h: Built on sacrifice, sustained by community
passages.t: How PHICA works.
With no major donor or grant, the founders gave portions of their own salaries to pay teachers and keep the doors open.
A substantial number of pupils attend tuition-free or receive significant financial help. Poverty should never be a permanent sentence on a child's future.
Families who can contribute pay US$60 or less (Nursery – Grade 6). Contributions from families who can afford them help keep education accessible to those who cannot.

passages.h: More than lessons: growing whole children
passages.t: Our mission. We want our pupils to grow academically, socially, morally and personally: to value health, hygiene, responsibility, cooperation, respect, integrity, compassion and service. A school close to home reduces the need for young children to make long, costly or unsafe journeys to learn. Improving access to elementary education. Strengthening foundational literacy and numeracy. Supporting children from vulnerable households. Promoting health, hygiene and child well-being. Building community resilience after Ebola.

passages.h: More than lessons: growing whole children
passages.t: Reducing educational inequality.

Behind every need is a child. PHICA still runs on limited resources without substantial external support. As enrollment grows, so do the needs. A request for furniture means a child who deserves a proper place to sit. A request for textbooks means a child who should not learn without a book. A scholarship means a child who doesn't have to leave school because their family can't pay. Classroom infrastructure. Qualified, trained teachers. Teacher professional development. Textbooks & instructional materials. Furniture & classroom equipment.

Science & technology resources. Sanitation & water facilities. Library & reading resources. Scholarships for vulnerable children. School administration systems. Joy on the school grounds. Donated shoes and supplies. Back-to-school packages.

passages.h: Every child deserves an opportunity to learn, regardless of family circumstances or economic status.
passages.t: Our enduring principle. For us, this is not simply a statement. It is the reason the school exists. The founders began this journey with what they had. With the right partners, we can do much more together.
Your information. How TIME Inc. handles the information you share through this website, our contact form and TIME Learning.

The public website uses no cookies, no advertising and no tracking or analytics tools . We only receive personal information that you choose to send us: through the contact form, by WhatsApp, phone or email, or by creating a TIME Learning account. We use it to answer you, to run our courses and to keep records of your learning. We do not sell it or share it for marketing. You can ask us to see, correct or delete your information at any time.

The website is hosted by GitHub Pages (GitHub, Inc.). Like any web host, GitHub automatically receives technical information such as your IP address and browser type when you load a page, and may keep it in security logs. We cannot see these logs and do not use them. Fonts and images are served from the website itself, so loading a page does not contact Google or other third parties. Links to WhatsApp, Google Maps and other sites only connect you to those services when you choose to follow them; their own privacy policies then apply.

The TIME Assistant chat answers from information published on this website. What you type in it stays in your browser (kept only until you close the tab) and is not sent to us or anyone else, unless you tap a WhatsApp or contact link to ask us directly.

When you send a message through our contact form , we receive your name, email address, phone or WhatsApp number (if you give it), the topic you choose and your message . The form is delivered by FormSubmit (formsubmit.co), a form-forwarding service, to the TIME Inc. office inbox at tinstitute312@gmail.com, which is a Google Gmail account. We use your details only to reply to you and to follow up on your request, such as a course registration, donation or partnership. If the form cannot send, the website offers to open your own email app or WhatsApp with your message instead. Nothing is sent until you choose to send it there.

If you contact us by WhatsApp, phone or email, we receive your number or email address and whatever you tell us. WhatsApp messages are handled by WhatsApp (Meta) under its own terms. We use these conversations only to respond to you and to provide the service you asked about.

If you create an account on TIME Learning , we store the information needed to run your courses: Account details: your name and email address. Passwords and sign-in are handled by Neon Auth, our account provider; we never see your password. A one-time code is emailed to you to confirm your address. Course records: course requests and approvals, your cohort, lessons you mark complete, quiz and test answers and results, written submissions and any files you upload, grades and lecturer feedback, and class attendance recorded by staff.

Support requests: the questions you send through the support centre and the replies. Activity records: a log of important account and teaching actions (for example approvals and grade changes), kept for security and to resolve disputes. Message contents are not included in this log. This information is stored in a private database run by Neon on Amazon Web Services servers in Frankfurt, Germany . It is visible only to you, to the lecturers assigned to your courses (for those courses), and to TIME administrators. Administrators can export course reports for TIME staff use only.
The free study guides on TIME Learning save your notes and progress in your own browser on your device. They are not sent to us unless you choose to save a copy to your account.

We do not sell personal information or share it for advertising. We only share it: with the service providers named above (GitHub, FormSubmit, Google Gmail, Neon and its email delivery, WhatsApp), only so they can provide their service to us; with the Ministry of Education or other authorities where the law requires it, for example for accredited teacher-training records; with your permission, for example to confirm your certificate to an employer you name.

We keep contact messages for as long as we need them to answer and follow up on your request. We keep learning records for as long as needed to provide your course and to confirm your training and results afterwards. You can ask us to delete information we no longer need.

You can ask us to see a copy of , correct or delete your personal information, or to stop contacting you. Contact us using the details below. We will confirm your identity before acting on a request, and we will tell you if we must keep some records, for example results that confirm a certificate.

This website and TIME Learning are intended for adults: teachers, professionals, parents, donors and partners. Information about pupils of Phìtìa Academy is handled by the school directly and is not collected through this website.

The website and TIME Learning use encrypted connections (HTTPS). TIME Learning checks every request against your verified account, and lecturers can only reach the courses assigned to them. No system is perfectly secure, so please do not upload medical records or other highly sensitive documents.

We will update this page if our practices change, and show the date of the latest version below. Questions or requests: email tinstitute312@gmail.com , call +231 777 891 104 , or write to TIME Inc., Phìtìa Academy (PHICA) campus, Slagbaawein Oldfield, Live Smart Community, Tower Hill, Robertsfield Highway, Margibi County, Liberia. Last updated: 24 October 2026.
Teacher education. An accredited teacher-training certificate that helps elementary teachers and subject specialists become skilled, ethical, professional classroom teachers.

Overview. Elementary school teachers who have not yet had formal teacher training. Subject specialists who know their subject and want to learn how to teach it. School staff preparing for an accredited teaching qualification.
Teaching methods for each subject area. Lesson planning and classroom management. Assessment of learners' progress. Professional ethics and educational leadership.

Duration · 9 months. Tuition · US$80 (LRD 13,600), in 2 installments of US$40. 2027 intake · Register by January 4, 2027 · classes begin March 8, 2027. Accreditation · Bureau of Teacher Education, Ministry of Education. Classes · Weekday afternoons and/or Saturdays.

Subject areas. Prepares elementary teachers in core subject areas and professional pedagogy. 01 Mathematics and Integrated Science. 02 Language Arts & Social Studies. 03 Early Childhood Education. 04 Geography and Government Studies.

passages.h: How much does this program cost?
passages.t: Tuition is US$80 (LRD 13,600) for the full nine-month program, paid in two equal installments of US$40 (LRD 6,800): the first when you register and the second before the exit examination. A registration fee of US$15 may apply, and the exit examination fee is US$10 (LRD 1,700).

passages.t: Tuition covers instruction only unless stated in writing; admissions will tell you before you enroll whether learning materials, exams, certificate processing or internship costs are extra. All tuition must be paid before the exit examination, and you should pay only through official TIME Inc. channels and keep your receipts.

Most programs offer a weekday track (Monday, Wednesday and Friday, 3:00 PM – 6:00 PM) and a Saturday track (8:00 AM – 3:00 PM). Schedules vary by program, so confirm the timetable for your course with admissions.

Blended program. Our first special training cohort: eight courses taught by qualified lecturers, studied 60% online through TIME Learning and 40% in person.
Overview. School leaders and administrators. Teachers supporting learners with different needs. Health and project professionals who want structured, blended study.
School leadership, policy and decision-making. Project planning, research and communication skills. Health care management and drug dispensing principles.
Duration · 10 weeks. Delivery · 60% online, 40% in person. Courses · 8, each with a named lecturer. Lecturers · Master's to PhD qualifications.

Courses and lecturers. A 10-week program delivered through 60% online and 40% in-person instruction. 01 School Leadership and Management Lecturer: Rev. Yekeku. 02 Leadership, Policy, and Decision-Making for School Administrators Lecturer: Dr. Saywrayne, III 03 Leadership, Policy, and Strategy Lecturer: Dr. Saywrayne, III. 04 Project Planning and Management Lecturer: AB Kekulah. 05 Research Skills Development Lecturer: Mr. Gbeh, Jr. 06 Standard English: Reading, Writing, and Public Speaking Lecturer: Dr. Toga. 07 Principles of Drug Dispensing Lecturer: Mr. Bee.
08 Health Care Management Lecturer: Mr. Kollie.
Delivery.
About 60% of the program is studied online in TIME Learning , where your lecturers publish lessons, quizzes, assignments and class dates. The other 40% is taught in person.
How to enrol.
Open TIME Learning , register as a student and verify your email address with the code we send you.
Choose the courses you want to join. Your request shows as pending until it is reviewed.
TIME reviews your request and approves your enrolment. Use Check approval in your account to see the decision.
Open each course to find lessons, quizzes, assignments, class dates and announcements from your lecturers.

Yes. TIME Inc. is an accredited supplementary teacher-training institution under the Bureau of Teacher Education, Ministry of Education (MoE), Liberia, and has been registered with the Government of Liberia since January 2021.

passages.h: How much does this program cost?
passages.t: Please contact admissions for the fee and payment arrangements for the Special Education Support Training.

passages.h: How does the online part work?
passages.t: You study the online part in TIME Learning: create a student account, verify your email address and request enrolment. Once TIME approves your enrolment, your lessons, quizzes, assignments and class schedule appear in your account. The in-person classes take place with your lecturers.

passages.h: When does the next cohort start?
passages.t: Contact admissions for the start date of the next Special Education Support Training cohort. More answers in our FAQ.
